scope_notes: HISTORICAL SNAPSHOT: this inventory predates the final queue upgrades. The user reports that the auth agent now covers all nine subscription queue message keys and the proposal fallback with a reusable operational notice component. Historical findings below do not describe current live gaps.
No code, gallery, template, deployment or other repository file edited by this audit. No application modules imported or executed, no network or production calls made.
Active means source-wired or callable; source presence, workflow names, dispatch labels and registry entries do not prove live execution.
Shared worktree has concurrent changes. File hashes record the contents read; source lines may shift after other agents edit.
Root TSX templates, reference previews, provider HTML, custom bodies, direct SMTP transports, durable queues and workflow-only payloads are counted separately.
Database contents, externally deployed n8n workflows, provider dashboard templates and production activation are unverified.

summary.coverage_claim: The request covers ALL email paths. The observed baseline contains 40 root company templates, all registered, plus 10 reference previews and 4 native auth templates. Counts and queue-path findings describe the source snapshot before the final queue upgrades; they are not current live gaps.

source_groups.scope: All physical root TSX email templates, not just the ten reference previews.
Ten existing named designs, registered through preview metadata; no production sendEmail caller found.
Provider-owned confirmation, recovery, invitation and magic-link HTML; another agent owns changes.
Source call sites, not confirmed production traffic. sendEmail renders the supplied React element; registry is preview metadata.
Seven queue insertion sites yield nine template keys and text-only records; no direct SMTP send.
Every checked-in workflow graph parsed; actual remote workflow activation not inspected.
No email transport, SMTP library or email enqueue path found; PDF/email contact labels and social publishing are not email sends.

raw_paths.flow: Root React template -> React Email render -> claimOutbox -> SMTP sendMail (unless suppressed, dry-run, duplicate or unconfigured).
raw_paths.notes: The final html field is rendered React Email, not a separate raw HTML authoring path. templateKey is recorded, not resolved through the registry.

raw_paths.flow: Existing pending/retrying row -> claim -> HTML presence check -> SMTP using row.html unchanged.
raw_paths.notes: Worker does not render a registry key or wrap stored HTML. Existing queued HTML remains unchanged by source template migration; production rows were not inspected.

raw_paths.flow: Fresh proposal approval -> enqueueEmail(metadata only) -> escaped subject paragraph + metadata pre -> claimOutbox processing row -> stale-processing recovery -> stored HTML SMTP worker.
raw_paths.notes: Actual caller does not supply html. Fallback HTML is authored outside shared templates. enqueueEmail does not send; claimOutbox starts processing rather than pending, so this path depends on stuck-row recovery for later dispatch.

raw_paths.flow: Maintenance order/payment/activation/refund/expiry or correction request -> direct email_outbox.insert with text and template_key but no html -> worker rejects as missing rendered body.
raw_paths.notes: Nine template keys at seven insertion sites. They are not successfully sending raw emails under the checked-in worker; adding registry preview entries alone does not make these rows render.

raw_paths.flow: Default or admin-supplied campaign HTML -> outreach_sequence_steps.body_html -> cron personalization -> OutreachSequenceEmail bodyHtml -> shared EmailLayout -> sendEmail -> SMTP.
raw_paths.notes: This is a real potential send when activated and not dry-run. Raw body bypasses semantic React content components, but it retains the registered template shell and shared transport. Four default HTML bodies exist at lines 5, 13, 21 and 29.

raw_paths.flow: Auth SDK call -> Supabase Auth -> configured provider HTML template -> provider SMTP.
raw_paths.notes: Four local HTML templates. Local config disables signup confirmations; provider runtime and production configuration were not queried. Recovery/invitation calls remain source-visible. No magic-link SDK call found in src at this snapshot.

raw_paths.flow: Workflow code returns subject/body/notification payloads -> signed HTTP callback. Repository callback updates automation_events status only; no sendEmail, outbox insert or SMTP call.
raw_paths.notes: No Email Send/Gmail/provider transport nodes or provider send code found in the scanned workflow graphs. QUEUED_FOR_OUTBOUND_SMTP, report_dispatched and dispatchedAt are payload labels, not delivery evidence. The callback accepts processed/failed; workflow-specific status strings such as report_dispatched are rejected if this callback is the configured target.

raw_paths.flow: ReferenceButton constructs Outlook VML + normal anchor inside ReferenceFrame.
raw_paths.notes: Raw HTML here is email-client button markup, not an independent email sender.

non_sender_paths.notes: Publish tools target Discord, Telegram, website DB, Meta, LinkedIn and X; no SMTP or email-send implementation found.
Returns rendered PDF bytes; template contact addresses and references to a welcome email are document content.
recordProviderSendReceipt/markMessageCompleted validate a supplied receipt and update state. The gmail/smtp/resend enum does not implement delivery.
No source callers of STANDARD_NURTURE_SEQUENCE or shouldSuppressFollowUp found; five templateId labels are not active email templates.

verification.method: TypeScript/TSX AST parsing of imports, registry entries and send/enqueue calls; JSON graph parsing for all workflow files; text search for SMTP/provider/Python/SQL email bypasses; source-only flow inspection.
